newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine wealth tax won't scare off capital-Menem.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wealth tax won't scare off capital-Menem.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem promised Monday to subject proposals to double personal wealth tax to close scrutiny in order to avoid scaring capital away from the country.

Menem is trying to push through Congress a new tax package to help bridge the budget deficit. But he was reported to have promised a business conference Friday he would block attempts by deputies from his own Peronist Party to double the tax on assets of over $102,000 to 1.0 percent from 0.5 percent.

"We have to study this very deeply to avoid injustices and of course to head off the possibility of capital leaving or not coming to Argentina because of unconsulted measures," the president told ATC state television.
"We have to see what we tax, whether we tax a factory that already pays tax or machinery, or just luxury goods," he said.

Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, trying to head off a budget gap he said could hit $6.6 billion this year, promised to share the wealth tax with the provinces instead of revenues from his new fuel taxes -- a much more liquid source of cash.
But Peronist deputies on the Budget and Finance Committee of the lower house of Congress defied Fernandez last week by proposing to the double the tax when they debate the bill.

Local business leaders reacted with alarm and the head of the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, Julio Macchi, called it "a blow to the very foundations of our capital market", since the base of the wealth tax includes stock holdings.
"I prefer a rate of 0.5 percent," Fernandez told La Nacion newspaper Sunday.

Peronist deputy Humberto Roggero, head of lower house's Industry Committee, said Monday he would propose that if the wealth tax is doubled, the taxable base should be raised to $250,000 from $102,000 -- "a more logical level."
Roggero said he would also propose that "productive" assets such as factories and machinery, and stock and bond holdings, be exempt from the personal wealth tax.
